Question ID: STAT_U05_L07_QZ_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.INF.7

A simulation shows differences from -2 to 2 are common, but the observed difference is 8. What does this suggest?

answer.text: The observed difference is unusual under the model

feedback.text: An observed difference far outside the simulated range may be statistically meaningful.

answer.text: The difference is always caused by bias

feedback.text: Bias is possible in some studies, but the simulation result itself points to unusual evidence.

answer.text: The model is automatically perfect

feedback.text: An unusual result challenges the model rather than proving it perfect.

answer.text: No conclusion can ever be made

feedback.text: The simulation gives evidence that can support a cautious conclusion.

Question ID: STAT_U05_L07_QZ_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.DMC.1

Which feature makes a statistical report more trustworthy?

answer.text: It uses a large headline only

feedback.text: A headline alone does not show statistical quality.

answer.text: It hides the graph scale

feedback.text: Hiding scale can make a graph misleading.

answer.text: It explains the sampling method and supports conclusions with data

feedback.text: A trustworthy report explains methods and connects claims to evidence.

answer.text: It claims causation from any association

feedback.text: Causation requires an appropriate design, usually a randomized experiment.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U05_L07_QZ_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.INF.7

What is practical significance?

answer.text: Whether a difference is large enough to matter in context

feedback.text: Practical significance asks whether the size of the effect matters.

answer.text: Whether all samples are identical

feedback.text: Samples vary; identical samples are not required.

answer.text: Whether a graph has bright colors

feedback.text: Visual design does not determine practical importance.

answer.text: Whether the sample size is zero

feedback.text: A sample size of zero gives no useful evidence.
